items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: I always thought ECM records were some of the, especially in the present day, were some of the more better and beautifully recorded recordings. I think I also love Blue Note records and Columbia records, but you know, I never was too crazy about CTI... I mean maybe it’s stylistically, what that guy

ctx.x: Apparently he didn’t like the ECM sound too much.

He didn’t like ECM. Well it’s too bad for him. I mean also I don’t think, I mean in a way ECM, you know I mean people talk about that, it’s just, I mean ECM was a recording label before I went on it, I mean they were recording Jan Garbarek, they had recorded Keith Jarrett, they had recorded Ralph Towner, Eberhard Weber, European musicians. So it was starting to develop, it was just the beginning. The first records I think Paul Bley had a record, you know, and all of a sudden Manfred decided he’d like to record…

And I think after a while I think a lot of the recordings were done in particular studios, like you know Oslo or in Stuttgart, a lot of times they were done with similar musicians playing with each other, like I might be playing on a record with Kenny Wheeler and then there was Jack DeJohnette and then there’d be a Jack DeJohnette record that I would play on and then Jack would play with or Kenny would play with somebody else and Jan Garbarek would play and then I did a record with Jan Garbarek. And you know did…
